newsitem.title: USA: Charleston, W.Va., extends excess property tax.
newsitem.headline: Charleston, W.Va., extends excess property tax.

text.p: Voters in Charleston, W.Va., approved a three-year extension of a property tax excess levy that raises $46 million a year, the city clerk's office said Monday.
The proposal won approval from more than 85 percent of the 4,260 voters who cast ballots Saturday.

It was the second time in four months the extension has gone before Charleston voters. It needed at least 60 percent approval to pass but garnered only 50 percent when it was placed on the general electon ballot in November.
The city has levied the tax of about 10 cents per $100 of assessed property value for 63 years. It must be renewed by referendum every three years.
Revenues from the excess levy go into the city's general fund and are used for a variety of services, including police and fire protection and trash pickup.
